On the night of 15 January 1902, the young Abdulaziz ibn Saud, later called Ibn Saud, took Riyadh from the governor of the rival Rashidi family with a small band of about forty men.

His family had been driven out in 1891 and lived in exile in Kuwait. The raiders climbed into the town at night and waited for the governor, Ajlan, to come out of the Masmak fort at dawn. They killed him at the gate, and the garrison gave up.

Saudis count this as the founding act of their state. Over the next three decades Ibn Saud took the rest of Najd, the east coast and the Hejaz, in the unification of Saudi Arabia. The Masmak fort is now a museum.
sum: On the night of 15 January 1902, the young Abdulaziz ibn Saud, later called Ibn Saud, took Riyadh from the governor of the rival Rashidi family with a small band of about forty men.
